title: Education is a widely valued American-Dream institution whose perceived school performance tracks opportunity hope
source_unit: Milken Center for Advancing the American Dream and Gallup American Dream Study, second wave
geography: United States; nationally representative survey of more than 6,300 adults, fielded January 7-March 4, 2026

observations.period: January 7-March 4, 2026; education as part of the American Dream

denominator.unit: more than 6,300 U.S. adults surveyed in the MCAAD-Gallup American Dream Study

quality_education_dream.unit: percent saying obtaining a quality education is a very or somewhat important part of the American Dream

very_important_education.unit: percent saying quality education is very important to the American Dream

future_priority.value: Education and learning rank third among areas Americans say the U.S. should prioritize over the next 50 years to expand opportunity for future generations.

education_as_social_contract.value: Education functions as a cultural promise connecting present institutions to future mobility, work opportunity and intergenerational fairness.

observations.method: Second wave of the nationally representative MCAAD-Gallup American Dream Study, conducted by web and mail among more than 6,300 U.S. adults from January 7-March 4, 2026.
observations.uncertainty: The public article does not provide the exact sample size, full weighting details or respondent-level linkage between school experiences and Dream judgments; the study is observational.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults, with comparisons by age, parent status, education, political party and financial circumstances.
observations.counterinterpretation: Education may be a symbolic expression of broader opportunity ideals rather than a direct evaluation of schools; respondents may value education even while distrusting current institutions.

observations.period: January 7-March 4, 2026; importance-performance gap in K-12 goals

denominator.unit: more than 6,300 U.S. adults surveyed; goal-specific denominators follow the study question

critical_thinking_gap.value: 88% call teaching critical thinking and problem-solving very important, while 17% rate K-12 schools excellent or very good on that goal

life_improvement_gap.value: 79% call giving everyone a chance to improve life circumstances very important, while 18% rate school performance excellent or very good

workforce_preparation_gap.value: 77% call workforce preparation very important, while 16% rate schools excellent or very good on it

institutional_bargain_gap.value: Large gaps between what education is expected to deliver and what schools are perceived to deliver can weaken confidence in opportunity institutions even when their cultural value remains high.

observations.method: Descriptive importance and performance ratings from the MCAAD-Gallup survey across five K-12 goals.
observations.uncertainty: Ratings are public perceptions, not classroom observations, achievement measures, causal school evaluations or evidence about individual student outcomes.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults; ratings vary by age, parent status, education and direct connection to schools.
observations.counterinterpretation: Respondents may hold higher standards for national institutions than for their local schools, and low ratings may reflect general political dissatisfaction or media narratives rather than school operations.

observations.period: January 7-March 4, 2026; school ratings and American-Dream optimism

denominator.unit: more than 6,300 U.S. adults surveyed; favorable-rating subgroup defined by rating at least three of five school goals excellent or very good

favorable_school_optimism.unit: percent of adults with favorable school ratings who agree they are optimistic about the future of the American Dream

other_school_optimism.unit: percent among adults not giving favorable ratings on at least three goals

everyone_opportunity.value: 61% of favorable-ratings group versus 43% of others agree everyone has opportunity to achieve the Dream

next_generation.value: 68% of favorable-ratings group versus 40% of others agree the next generation will have more opportunities

association_boundary.value: The reported link persists after accounting for age, education, party, financial circumstances and general optimism, but remains an observational association rather than a demonstrated school effect.

observations.method: Gallup summary of adjusted and unadjusted associations between K-12 ratings and American-Dream optimism; full model details are provided in a linked appendix.
observations.uncertainty: The public article does not establish temporal order, causal direction, unmeasured family or community factors, or whether improving school performance would increase Dream optimism.
observations.subgroup: Adults rating schools favorably on at least three of five goals versus those who do not.
observations.counterinterpretation: Optimistic people may rate institutions more favorably, or both ratings may reflect local conditions, socioeconomic security, political identity or direct school connection.

related_sources.claim: Official Gallup article reports MCAAD-Gallup sample, education importance, K-12 goals, importance-performance gaps, subgroup patterns and Dream-optimism associations.

boundary: This record adds an education-to-opportunity-legitimacy route from cultural valuation of quality education through perceived K-12 performance, intergenerational hope and institutional confidence. It does not establish school effectiveness, causal effects on optimism, student achievement, classroom conditions or policy impact.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Gallup article was reviewed for survey frame, sample and field dates, education importance, five K-12 goals, importance-performance gaps, personal/direct-connection differences, favorable-rating subgroup comparisons and association caveats.
